title: The story mountain: how a plot rises and falls
examples: What is the climax of a story?
How do I plan a story with a story mountain?

explain.say: Have you ever climbed a hill? You walk up, up, up, reach the top, then come down the other side. Many stories have exactly that shape! Look at the line on the board. It is a story mountain. At the start, the opening, things are calm and low.

draw.text: The story mountain: how a plot rises and falls

explain.say: See the line climbing? That is the build-up. Something starts to go wrong and the excitement rises. Your heart beats faster as you read. What makes you want to turn the page?
Now look at the very top of the mountain: the climax. That is the most exciting moment, when the problem is at its worst. Will the hero escape? Can you think of a climax from a film you love?

After the top, the line comes down. The problem gets sorted out, which is called the resolution, and at the ending everything is calm again. Look at the board: here is a real story, The Monkey and the Crocodile, from the Panchatantra in India. Spot the climax?

explain.say: You are a story mountaineer! Look back at the whole mountain: opening, build-up, climax, resolution and ending. Writers all over the world use it to plan. Challenge: draw a mountain and plan a story about a lost puppy.

faq.a: A story mountain is a plan shaped like a hill: the opening, the build-up, the climax at the top, then the resolution and the ending on the way down.

faq.q: What is the climax of a story?
faq.a: The climax is the most exciting or tense moment, at the top of the story mountain, when the problem is at its worst.
asks: What does climax mean in a story?

faq.q: What happens in the opening of a story?
faq.a: The opening introduces the main character, where the story happens and when. Things are usually calm.
asks: How does a story mountain start?

faq.a: The resolution is where the problem is solved, on the way down the mountain, just before the ending.

faq.q: How do I plan a story with a story mountain?
faq.a: Draw the mountain and write one note at each point: opening, build-up, climax, resolution, ending. Then turn each note into a paragraph.

facts: The Panchatantra, a collection of animal fables from ancient India, is more than 1,500 years old.
A German writer, Gustav Freytag, drew plot as a pyramid in 1863, an idea behind the story mountain.
